name: Bubble Break ASMR
request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

assetNeeds.constraints: Must retain Marketplace provenance and pass loading, native playback, and listening checks. It must be a short, clean, satisfying close-up pop appropriate for repeated ASMR interaction, with no speech, music, weapon character, excessive reverb, or long tail. Playback must synchronize with the visible rupture phase and occur once per accepted pop. Built-in, generated, procedural, placeholder, or invented asset IDs are forbidden.

spec.assetStrategy: Discovery begins with a complete interactive bubble-wrap Model rather than a static prop. The selected candidate must be inspected for scripts, hierarchy, dependencies, geometry, per-bubble state, input handling, animation phases, counter/reset interfaces, embedded sounds, and cleanup before missing implementation or glue ownership is assigned. Verified useful behavior, animation, geometry, and media will be preserved. The separate Audio need is mandatory even if the sound is captured from the retained component, because its provenance, loading, playback, synchronization, and listening quality still require native verification. If supported Marketplace discovery and inspection finds no suitable complete component, only the evidenced missing portions may be authored; an importer or serialization limitation is instead recorded and escalated and does not authorize stripping or replacing an otherwise suitable scripted component. No asset IDs will be invented. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; compatible animation must arrive in a reusable Model, while any authored timing is decided only after component inspection. All imported and authored instances, dependencies, and eventual glue remain inside Forge_25080204687e.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR
spec.summary:
A compact single-player bubble-popping experience centered on a close tabletop sheet. The chosen default is a readable 4-by-4 sheet, giving sixteen individual bubbles and exceeding the requested minimum of twelve. At spawn, the player is safely positioned at the near edge of a small bounded tabletop alcove with the bubble sheet filling the main view, a warm task light above it, and an unobtrusive counter/reset HUD. No travel through a large map is required: the player can immediately click or tap a visible bubble, with limited room to adjust viewing angle around the near side of the table.

Each accepted press has observable phases: a quick depression, a visible rupture synchronized to verified Marketplace pop audio, and a short settle into a clearly collapsed state. The server-authoritative bubble state locks when a press is accepted, so holding, rapid repeat presses, overlapping input, and presses on popped bubbles cannot produce another sound or count. Exactly one is added only after that bubble's pop sequence completes. The counter progresses from 0/16 to 16/16, then clear but restrained completion feedback identifies the finished sheet. Nothing resets automatically; the player deliberately activates the reset control to restore all bubbles and return the counter to zero while interaction is temporarily locked.

There is no persistence, economy, purchase flow, combat, progression tree, or multiplayer-dependent mechanic. State is fresh for the current play session and cleaned up on departure or character replacement. Marketplace inspection decides how much existing component behavior can be retained and what glue is genuinely missing. Native desktop and touch play sessions—not code inspection—must verify targeting, timing, synchronized audible playback, exact counting, completion, reset, respawn handling, and the absence of duplicate awards.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a calm, close-focus tabletop ASMR composition rather than a broad environment. The central focal point is a compact rectangular translucent bubble-wrap sheet on a matte warm-wood or neutral craft table. Sixteen bubbles form an evenly spaced 4-by-4 grid with rounded, soft silhouettes and generous target separation. Unpopped bubbles should catch a cool translucent highlight; busy bubbles visibly compress; popped bubbles remain flattened, slightly desaturated, and unmistakably different without relying only on color.

Frame the play area as a small desk alcove: safe near-side spawn, central work surface, warm directional task lamp, simple backboard or wall, and low side boundaries that prevent falling while leaving the sheet unobstructed. The sheet should be reachable and readable immediately from spawn, with only a short step or camera adjustment needed. Decorative objects, if any, stay sparse and peripheral so they do not compete with individual hit targets. Avoid a featureless baseplate, oversized room, distant camera, visual clutter, or unrelated props.

Use a restrained palette: warm wood and cream surroundings, cool clear-blue bubble highlights, charcoal text, and one muted accent for actionable reset/completion states. Lighting should emphasize curved bubble highlights and depressed silhouettes without harsh bloom. Pop feedback should be tactile and localized: fast downward compression, rupture at the audio transient, a short settle, and a subtle local highlight or ripple only if supported by the retained component. Completion feedback may use a brief soft sheet-wide sheen and a concise message, not confetti or spectacle.

The HUD is minimal and touch-readable: a compact counter such as “Popped 0 / 16” in a top corner and one clearly separated Reset Sheet control with adequate touch target size. Completion changes the message to “Sheet complete” and makes the fresh-sheet action obvious, while preserving the counter. UI must respect common desktop and mobile safe areas, avoid covering the sheet, provide visible pressed/disabled states, and remain legible against the scene.

tasks.title: Search, import, and audit complete reusable bubble-wrap interactions, preserving verified geometry, sources, animation, behavior, media, and interfaces; record unsupported importer or dependency capabilities without substituting a procedural replacement.

Audit captured component sounds first, then search separately if necessary, and retain a Marketplace pop sound only after provenance, loading, playback, synchronization suitability, and listening checks pass.

After component inspection establishes its interfaces, preserve existing interaction behavior and add only missing authoritative per-bubble locking, completion-timed counting, validation, and reset transitions; assign exclusive glue script paths at that point.
Compose the compact bounded tabletop alcove, safe spawn, close readable sheet placement, task lighting, and unobstructed interaction area around the retained component.
Preserve or complete the observable depression, rupture, synchronized audio, settled-pop, sheet-completion, and fresh-sheet restoration presentation after auditing retained animation and media.
After retained interfaces are known, add only missing persistent counter/reset presentation and desktop/touch input glue, with initial-state synchronization, safe-area layout, and respawn rebinding.
Integrate sixteen-bubble completion detection, restrained completion feedback, deliberate nonautomatic reset, and clean restoration of every bubble and counter state.
Review session initialization, character replacement, connection cleanup, player departure, and namespace isolation without adding persistence or multiplayer-dependent mechanics.

Run protected native desktop and touch gameplay verification for targeting, press/pop/settle timing, heard synchronized Marketplace audio, spam resistance, exact counting, completion, reset, respawn, and required-object presence; report any untestable or blocked claim honestly.
